articles.title: A doorbell camera's battery is drained by how often it wakes, not by how long it is on
articles.excerpt: Battery capacity is the number every doorbell camera is sold on, and it is the number that explains the least about how long the product actually lasts between charges. A 5000 mAh cell sounds like it…
articles.body: Battery capacity is the number every doorbell camera is sold on, and it is the number that explains the least about how long the product actually lasts between charges. A 5000 mAh cell sounds like it should give you a predictable number of weeks, and then the first month in a busy doorway gives you half of what you expected. Nothing is faulty. The capacity was never the variable that mattered. The camera is asleep almost all the time A battery doorbell spends the overwhelming majority of its life in a low-power state where the imaging path is off and only a motion sensor is listening. It is not recording, it is not streaming, and it is not holding a full Wi-Fi session. This is the only reason a battery doorbell is possible at all.
articles.author: Xingliao Smart Home

articles.title: Why a Twitter/X character counter can't just use JavaScript .length
articles.excerpt: When you're writing for X, one character is not always one counted unit. JavaScript strings use UTF-16; visual glyphs can span several code points; and X's public weighted-character rules treat many C…
articles.body: When you're writing for X, one character is not always one counted unit. JavaScript strings use UTF-16; visual glyphs can span several code points; and X's public weighted-character rules treat many CJK characters and emoji differently from Latin text. Three examples make the difference clear: "Hello world" is 11 weighted characters. "中文" has 2 visible glyphs but a weighted length of 4. " https://example.com " typically has a fixed recognized URL weight of 23, not its literal text length. Using str.length on the whole message misses all of this.

articles.body: Most guides to taking crypto in WooCommerce start the same way: create an account with a payment processor, upload your company documents, wait for a review, then install their plugin and paste in an API key. The plugin is the easy part. The account is what slows you down, and it's also the thing that can be closed later. This walkthrough takes a different route. The plugin talks to a payment server you run yourself, so there's no account to apply for. I'll use Coldtill , the gateway we build, and its WooCommerce plugin. It's a short job, but there are a few details (store currency, webhook URLs, partial payments) that are worth knowing before a real customer finds them for you.

articles.title: GitHub Octoverse 2026: What 7.38 Billion Monthly Commits Reveal About Agent-Generated Code at Scale
articles.excerpt: GitHub's 2026 Octoverse report shows commits jumped from roughly 2 billion to 7.38 billion per month. Merged pull requests tripled to 220 million per month. New repositories doubled to 30.3 million pe…
articles.body: GitHub's 2026 Octoverse report shows commits jumped from roughly 2 billion to 7.38 billion per month. Merged pull requests tripled to 220 million per month. New repositories doubled to 30.3 million per month. Most of this growth happened in the second half of 2026, and GitHub attributes it to developers building with agents. This is the first platform-level dataset that quantifies what happens when coding agents hit production scale. The numbers expose infrastructure stress points that every platform hosting agent-generated code will face: CI/CD bottlenecks, storage growth, merge conflict resolution, and rate limiting. The Infrastructure Shift When commit volume triples in under a year without a proportional increase in human developers, the platform's assumptions break.

articles.title: Deep Agents: How LangChain's Batteries-Included Harness Wires Sub-Agents, Filesystem Backends, and Persistent Memory
articles.excerpt: LangChain just shipped Deep Agents as their answer to "how do I actually deploy an agent?" It's an opinionated harness that runs out of the box with sub-agents, filesystem abstraction, persistent memo…
articles.body: LangChain just shipped Deep Agents as their answer to "how do I actually deploy an agent?" It's an opinionated harness that runs out of the box with sub-agents, filesystem abstraction, persistent memory, and human-in-the-loop approval. The project sits at 30,823 stars and is trending #5 on GitHub for Python. This is not a framework. It's a working agent you extend, override, or replace piece by piece. The interesting parts are how sub-agents isolate context, how the filesystem abstraction handles local vs. sandboxed vs. remote backends, how persistent memory bridges sessions, and what "batteries-included" means for production deployment (streaming, checkpointing, human approval).

articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine . What I Built You open a tutorial for your assignment. Then another tab. Then a video that has absolutely nothing to do with the assignment. Somewhere in the browser, a little teddy bear is still waiting for you. Butu is a focus companion for Chrome and Firefox that slowly haunts the pages you get distracted by. You tell him what you're working on, choose a time, and press “Let's do it together!” A small open-weight model runs inside the browser to work out whether the page you're reading belongs to that task. While you stay on task, Butu leaves you alone. One task, a little time, and someone to sit beside you Wander off, and he starts drawing in the margins of the page you're reading.

articles.title: India launches next-gen navigation satellite to orbit (video)
articles.excerpt: India launched the NVS-03 navigation satellite to orbit today (Oct. 30) atop a GSLV rocket. It was the fourth orbital launch from Indian soil so far this year.
articles.body: India bolstered its homegrown satellite-navigation system today (Oct. 30). A GSLV Mark II rocket launched the nation's NVS-03 satellite from Satish Dhawan Space Centre today at 2:21 p.m. EDT (1821 GMT and 11:51 p.m. India Standard Time). Everything went well: The rocket deployed NVS-03 into geostationary transfer orbit as planned, officials with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) announced on X about 30 minutes after liftoff. An Indian GSLV Mark II rocket launches the NVS-03 navigation satellite on Oct. 30, 2026. (Image credit: ISRO) NVS-03 is the third next-gen satellite that India has launched for the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), its version of the United States' Global Positioning System ( GPS ).

articles.body: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic say they will adopt a new standard that publishers can use to opt out of being scraped by AI, as reported earlier by Search Engine Roundtable . With this control, publishers can apply their AI training preferences across multiple AI companies, instead of setting them individually. The shared "policy token" signal is proposed by Kevin Kelley, a technical lead for standards at Anthropic, as part of the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF).
